question: Who controls a difficult-to-replace bottleneck, and who captures its economics?

sources.summary: Coherent describes components and transceivers, InP expansion, qualification requirements and competing architectures.
Lumentum describes 100G/200G EMLs, integrated laser/modulator and high-volume manufacturing. Company positioning, not independent superiority evidence.
Fabrinet lists wafer processing, alignment, packaging, fiber connections and system testing.
AOI explains bringing laser fabrication, optical assembly and module production together. Company assertion, not proof of scarce capacity.

sources.locator: FY2025 10-K, Business, Competition, sales by application
sources.summary: IPG reports 85.7% of 2025 revenue from materials processing and competition from laser suppliers and non-laser methods.
Broadcom describes switch-integrated optical engines and a separate pluggable laser source.

companies.role: Lasers, components and finished transceivers; broad vertical integration.
companies.constraint: Qualified capacity and yields, not wafer diameter alone.
companies.proof_needed: Document qualified available capacity, customer alternatives and segment margin/FCF capture.
companies.alternatives: Other qualified component/module vendors; architectural move to CPO.
companies.falsifier: Capacity additions or buyer integration can compete away scarcity.

companies.role: Laser/component exposure; EML product evidence is stronger here than broad system comparisons.
companies.constraint: High-speed optical signal quality at production yield.
companies.proof_needed: Compare identical reach, lane speed, temperature and reliability specs with qualified alternatives.
companies.alternatives: COHR/AAOI only for overlapping products; alternative laser/modulator architectures.
companies.falsifier: A performance advantage may not survive qualification of another supplier.

companies.role: Manufacturing, precision alignment, packaging and test services.
companies.constraint: Repeatable assembly yield and customer-qualified throughput.
companies.proof_needed: Prove allocation, customer transfer/requalification costs, utilisation and retained economics.
companies.alternatives: Customer in-house production or other qualified assembly partners.
companies.falsifier: Complex assembly is not ownership of the customer's product IP or pricing.

companies.constraint: Yield, reliable delivery and qualified module capacity.
companies.proof_needed: Prove qualification, orders, ramp yield and cash conversion; test customer concentration.
companies.alternatives: Other qualified transceiver suppliers or changing optical architectures.
companies.falsifier: More optical demand does not guarantee share gains or durable margins.

companies.role: Industrial fiber-laser exposure; not interchangeable with AI-network optics.
companies.constraint: Application-specific beam quality, uptime and total processing cost.
companies.proof_needed: Compare cost per accepted part and process qualification, not network bandwidth.
companies.alternatives: Coherent, nLight, Trumpf, Raycus and non-laser cutting/welding methods named in IPG filing.
companies.falsifier: Industrial pricing competition can offset technical progress.

scenarios.trigger: More traffic per rack and tighter energy budgets

steps.mechanism: Customers may require more or faster optical links.
steps.condition: Deployment architecture actually uses those links.
steps.falsifier: Network topology or utilisation reduces link count.

steps.mechanism: Qualified laser, alignment or test capacity may constrain delivered modules.
steps.condition: Demand exceeds usable qualified capacity, not announced capacity.
steps.falsifier: Yield improvements and competing supply absorb demand.

steps.mechanism: Suppliers may earn better mix or economics, or customers may capture the benefit.
steps.condition: Contracts and pricing let suppliers retain value after capex and working capital.
steps.falsifier: Price erosion, buyer bargaining power or cash-intensive ramps offset growth.

steps.mechanism: Optical engines move close to switch silicon.
steps.condition: Customers deploy the architecture at scale.
steps.falsifier: Serviceability, qualification or cost delays adoption.

steps.mechanism: Demand may move between pluggable modules, external lasers and precision packaging.
steps.condition: Specific bills of materials and supplier assignments change.
steps.falsifier: Existing suppliers adapt and retain content per system.

steps.mechanism: Profit may migrate to whichever layer controls qualification or scarce integration capacity.
steps.condition: That layer remains scarce and retains contractual economics.
steps.falsifier: Standardisation, dual sourcing or capacity expansion removes scarcity.

first_principles: Network optics: compare delivered bandwidth, energy per bit, reach, reliability and cost at qualified yield.
Industrial lasers: compare accepted parts per hour, precision, uptime and total processing cost.
Business capture requires scarcity, switching friction and retained cash economics; physical difficulty alone is insufficient.
